boundary_expansion.incremental_added_block: the added block uses the prompt-slot values plus "off"; only its LOWEST value counts as an edge ("off" lies beyond the highest)
boundary_expansion.order: (1) base grids for every head-to-head predictor, layer search, other-generator reference; (2) incremental comparisons with the base-round baselines; (3) decide expansions from (1) and (2); (4) evaluate the extra values, reselect layer and penalties; (5) rerun incremental comparisons against the reselected baselines with the expanded added-block grid
boundary_expansion.rule: if any predictor in a generator x objective selects the lowest or highest value of a tuned slot, that slot's grid is extended by one x10 step in that direction, once, for every predictor in that generator x objective that uses the slot; then everything is reselected. A winner on the extended edge is "best among the tested values".

common.folds: results/cv/folds.json (5 grouped folds over the 57 TRAIN groups, unchanged)

incremental.added_grid: prompt-slot values + off; off = strongest penalty under the tie rule (a tie goes to off); off reuses the baseline OOF predictions exactly
incremental.baseline: frozen at its head-to-head selection (penalties and, for B2, both slots)

common.layer_selection: H1 + structure over the candidate rows by the objective's pooled CV metric; reused for H1, H2, B1+H1, B2+H1 of that generator and objective
common.other_generator_reference: H1 + structure with the other generator's hidden states, the target generator's labels, structure, folds and recipe; its row chosen from its own candidates by the same rule
common.solver: damped modified Newton (factorised Hessian reused while max|grad| falls by at least 4x per step, refreshed otherwise or after a damped step), exact Hessian (float32 assembly on the Apple GPU when MIFE_V2_HESS=mps, else Accelerate; float64 Cholesky), float64 gradient; stop at max|grad| < 1e-9 (mean scale) or Newton decrement < 1e-14; warm start along the penalty path (strong -> weak); if the float32-assembled Hessian is numerically indefinite, the smallest diagonal jitter (1e-10 x mean diagonal, x10 steps) that permits Cholesky is added to that step only (logged per fit)
common.standardisation: per head, fitting rows only; constant columns scale 1
common.tie_rule: among settings whose rounded pooled loss equals the minimum, pick the largest sum of log10 tuned penalties; then the larger prompt penalty

objective1.heads: one ridge-logistic head per rule type (15) per generator and predictor
objective1.loss: summed binomial NLL on (violated, compliant) counts; implemented as mean per completion + penalty lam/N, N = head's fitting completions
objective1.selection_metric: pooled held-out mean log loss per completion (sum NLL / sum completions over every OOF row of every type and fold)

objective2.heads: one shared head per generator and predictor
objective2.loss: ridge fractional logit (binomial cross-entropy with q_hat as soft label, logistic link), every prompt weight 1; penalty lam/N, N = fitting prompts
objective2.selection_metric: pooled held-out mean squared error of the predicted fraction (every OOF prompt weight 1)
